short: Put the presidency at the centre of national life, at 42 the youngest to hold it.
full:
Roosevelt took the oath in a Buffalo house on 14 September 1901, hours after Leon Czolgosz's bullet killed William McKinley. At 42 he remains the youngest president, and he treated the office as what he called a bully pulpit, a platform for driving Congress rather than waiting on it.

He brought some forty antitrust suits, breaking up the Northern Securities railway combination in 1904, and intervened personally in the anthracite coal strike of 1902 on terms he called a Square Deal. The Pure Food and Drug Act and the Meat Inspection Act followed in 1906. He placed roughly 230 million acres under federal protection, backed the Panamanian revolt of 1903 to secure the canal zone, sent the Great White Fleet around the world, and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1906 for mediating an end to the Russo-Japanese War.
